question: A cyclist performing uniform circular motion throws an apple in his direction, the apple moves in a ____________.
option_1: tangential path to the circular path at that point
option_2: circular path opposite to the cyclist
option_3: straight line path opposite to the cyclist
solution_text:
The correct answer is tangential path to the circular path at that point.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The moment the apple leaves the cyclist's hand, no centripetal force acts on it anymore, so by Newton's first law of motion it stops following the circular path and moves in a straight line. (जड़त्व का नियम — वृत्तीय गति से मुक्त होते ही वस्तु सीधी रेखा में गति करती है)

 

• This straight line is directed along the tangent to the circle at the point of release, because the instantaneous velocity of any object in circular motion always points tangentially to the circle at that instant.

 

• 'Thrown in his direction' simply means the apple is released along the cyclist's own instantaneous velocity direction, which is itself tangential — so the apple's path after release is a straight tangential path, not another circle.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option A.

 

Additional Information

 

• In uniform circular motion, speed is constant but velocity keeps changing direction, so there is always a centripetal acceleration directed towards the centre.

 

• The centripetal force needed for circular motion is F = mv²/r, directed towards the centre of the circle.

 

• Common examples of tangential release: mud flying off a spinning bicycle tyre, a stone released from a sling — both fly off tangentially.

 

NOTE

 

• Circular path opposite to the cyclist (Option B): Wrong — once released, the apple has no force to keep it moving in a circle at all.

 

• Straight line path opposite to the cyclist (Option C): Wrong direction — the apple moves along the tangent, not opposite to the cyclist's motion.

 

• Circular path as the cyclist (Option D): Wrong — only the cyclist (under pedalling/steering force) continues circular motion; the free apple cannot.

question: While cleaning the school campus, students are asked to separate biodegradable waste. Which of the following should be placed in the biodegradable bin?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Wooden pencil shavings.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Biodegradable substances are those that can be broken down into simpler, harmless substances by the action of micro-organisms (bacteria and fungi) in nature. (जैव निम्नीकरणीय अपशिष्ट — सूक्ष्मजीवों द्वारा अपघटित होने वाला कचरा)

 

• Wooden pencil shavings are made of natural wood, an organic plant material, so decomposers can easily break them down — hence they are biodegradable.

 

• Polythene, metal cans and glass are all synthetic/inorganic materials which micro-organisms cannot break down, so they are non-biodegradable and must go in a separate bin for recycling or safe disposal.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option A.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other biodegradable items: fruit and vegetable peels, paper, cotton cloth, leaves, food waste.

 

• Other non-biodegradable items: plastics, thermocol, rubber, aluminium foil, most metals.

 

• Segregating waste at source into biodegradable (wet/green bin) and non-biodegradable (dry/blue bin) is a key step of Swachh Bharat Mission waste management guidelines.

 

NOTE

 

• Polythene bag (Option B): A synthetic plastic; takes hundreds of years to decompose, hence non-biodegradable.

 

• A crushed cold drink can (Option C): Made of aluminium/metal; not broken down by micro-organisms.

 

• Glass bottle (Option D): An inorganic material that does not decompose naturally; it is recyclable but not biodegradable.

question: Which of the following pairs of human male chromosome is mismatched in size?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sex chromosomes.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A human male has 23 pairs of chromosomes: 22 pairs of autosomes and 1 pair of sex chromosomes (XY). (लिंग गुणसूत्र — पुरुष में X व Y, आकार में असमान)

 

• In a male, the sex-chromosome pair is X and Y, and these two chromosomes are mismatched in size — the X chromosome is much larger than the Y chromosome, which is the smallest human chromosome.

 

• All 22 pairs of autosomes (including the 1st, 13th and 20th pairs) are homologous pairs, meaning the two chromosomes of each pair are matched in size and shape — this is true in both males and females.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option D.

 

Additional Information

 

• A human female has the sex-chromosome pair XX, which is a matched (homologous) pair, unlike in males.

 

• The Y chromosome carries the SRY gene, which triggers the development of male characteristics in the embryo.

 

• Sex of the child is determined by the father, since the mother always contributes an X chromosome, while the father contributes either an X (girl) or a Y (boy) chromosome.

 

NOTE

 

• Thirteenth pair autosomes (Option A): A normal homologous autosome pair, matched in size.

 

• First pair autosomes (Option B): The largest human chromosome pair, matched in size.

 

• Twentieth pair autosomes (Option C): Also a normal homologous, size-matched autosome pair.

question: According to Bohr's model of the atom, electrons in an atom:
option_1: are stationary in the atom and emit energy when struck by photons
option_2: are embedded in a positively charged sphere like plums in a pudding
option_3: revolve in fixed circular orbits and do not radiate energy while in these orbits
option_4: revolve around the nucleus in elliptical orbits and emit energy continuously
solution_text:
The correct answer is revolve in fixed circular orbits and do not radiate energy while in these orbits.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Bohr's model (1913) proposed that electrons revolve around the nucleus only in certain fixed circular orbits called energy levels or shells, and as long as an electron stays in a particular orbit, it does not radiate energy. (बोर मॉडल — निश्चित वृत्तीय कक्षाएँ, ऊर्जा का विकिरण नहीं)

 

• Energy is absorbed or emitted only when an electron jumps from one orbit to another — absorbing energy to jump to a higher orbit, and emitting a photon of energy when falling to a lower orbit.

 

• This model successfully explained the stability of the atom and the line spectrum of hydrogen, overcoming the flaw of earlier models which predicted electrons would spiral into the nucleus while radiating energy continuously.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option C.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Thomson model (plum pudding model) pictured the atom as a positively charged sphere with electrons embedded in it, like plums in a pudding.

 

• The Rutherford model, based on the alpha-particle scattering experiment, established that the atom has a small, dense, positively charged nucleus with electrons revolving around it — but could not explain why electrons don't spiral inward.

 

• Bohr's model was later refined by quantum mechanical model, which describes electrons in terms of probability clouds (orbitals) rather than fixed paths.

 

NOTE

 

• Stationary, emit energy when struck by photons (Option A): Not Bohr's model — electrons are never stationary; they are always revolving.

 

• Embedded in a positive sphere (Option B): This describes J.J. Thomson's plum pudding model, not Bohr's.

 

• Elliptical orbits emitting energy continuously (Option D): Elliptical orbits were introduced later by Sommerfeld; and continuous emission of energy would make the atom unstable, contrary to Bohr's postulate.

question: Which of the following is the compound produced by the action of chlorine on dry slaked lime (Ca(OH)2)?
solution_text:
The correct answer is bleaching powder.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• When chlorine gas is passed over dry slaked lime, Ca(OH)₂, it produces calcium oxychloride, CaOCl₂, commonly known as bleaching powder. (विरंजक चूर्ण — क्लोरीन व शुष्क बुझा चूना)

 

• Reaction: Ca(OH)₂ + Cl₂ → CaOCl₂ + H₂O.

 

• Bleaching powder is used for bleaching cotton and linen in the textile industry, bleaching wood pulp in paper factories, as an oxidising agent, and for disinfecting drinking water and swimming pools.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option D.

 

Additional Information

 

• Washing soda (Na₂CO₃·10H₂O) is obtained by heating baking soda, and is used in the glass, soap and paper industries and for removing water hardness.

 

• Common salt (NaCl) is obtained from sea water by evaporation and is the raw material for making washing soda, baking soda, and bleaching powder itself (via the chlor-alkali process).

 

• Baking soda (NaHCO₃), another important compound of sodium, is used in antacids and as a mild disinfectant.

 

NOTE

 

• Washing soda (Option A): Sodium carbonate decahydrate, a completely different compound with no chlorine.

 

• Bleaching soda (Option B): Not a standard chemical name; a distractor resembling 'bleaching powder' and 'washing soda'.

 

• Common salt (Option C): Sodium chloride, used as a raw material to manufacture bleaching powder via chlorine, but not itself the product of this reaction.

question: The generation of heat in a conductor due to electric current is known as:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Joule's heating.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• When current flows through a conductor having resistance, part of the electrical energy is converted into heat energy — this phenomenon is called Joule's heating effect or the heating effect of current. (जूल का तापन नियम — विद्युत धारा से ऊष्मा उत्पन्न होना)

 

• Joule's law of heating states that heat produced, H = I²Rt, where I is current, R is resistance and t is time — so heat is directly proportional to the square of the current.

 

• This principle is the working basis of devices such as the electric iron, electric heater, electric bulb (filament) and fuse wire.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option D.

 

Additional Information

 

• Ohm's Law states V = IR, relating voltage, current and resistance at constant temperature — it does not itself describe heat generation.

 

• Electromagnetic induction, discovered by Michael Faraday, is the production of an EMF (and hence current) in a conductor due to a changing magnetic field — the basis of generators and transformers.

 

• Electrolysis is the chemical decomposition of a substance by passing an electric current through its molten or aqueous solution form.

 

NOTE

 

• Ohm's Law (Option A): Relates current, voltage and resistance; unrelated to heat generation.

 

• Electromagnetic induction (Option B): Concerns generating current using a magnetic field, the reverse concept.

 

• Electrolysis (Option C): A chemical effect of current, used in electroplating and purification of metals, not the heating effect.

question: What is molecular mass of carbon dioxide?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: 44.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Molecular formula of carbon dioxide = CO₂. (कार्बन डाइऑक्साइड का आणविक द्रव्यमान)

 

• Atomic mass of carbon (C) = 12; atomic mass of oxygen (O) = 16.

 

• Molecular mass = 1×(mass of C) + 2×(mass of O) = 12 + 2×16 = 12 + 32 = 44 u.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option B.

 

Additional Information

 

• Molecular mass is the sum of the atomic masses of all atoms present in a molecule, expressed in atomic mass units (u).

 

• CO₂ is a colourless, odourless gas produced during respiration and combustion, and used by plants in photosynthesis.

 

• Some other common molecular masses: H₂O = 18, O₂ = 32, N₂ = 28, NH₃ = 17, CH₄ = 16.

 

NOTE

 

• 38 (Option A), 42 (Option C) and 22 (Option D) do not correspond to any correct calculation of C + 2O; only 12 + 32 = 44 is correct.

question: Which of the following is NOT present in animal cells?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chloroplast.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Chloroplasts are the green, chlorophyll-containing organelles found only in plant cells and some algae, where they carry out photosynthesis. (क्लोरोप्लास्ट — केवल पादप कोशिकाओं में)

 

• Since animal cells do not photosynthesise, they do not contain chloroplasts.

 

• Plasma membrane, nucleus and cytoplasm, on the other hand, are found in both plant and animal cells, being basic components common to almost all eukaryotic cells.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option C.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other structures present only in plant cells (and absent in animal cells): cell wall (made of cellulose) and a large central vacuole.

 

• Structures found only in animal cells (typically absent in plant cells): centrioles/centrosome and (in many animal cells) lysosomes in abundance.

 

• Both plant and animal cells contain mitochondria (the 'powerhouse of the cell'), the endoplasmic reticulum, Golgi apparatus and ribosomes.

 

NOTE

 

• Plasma membrane (Option A): The outer boundary of the cell, present in all cells, controlling entry/exit of substances.

 

• Nucleus (Option B): The control centre of the cell containing genetic material, present in both plant and animal cells.

 

• Cytoplasm (Option D): The jelly-like matrix inside the cell in which organelles are suspended, present in all cells.

question: Which of the following non-metals is found liquid at room temperature?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bromine.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Bromine (Br₂) is the only non-metal that exists in the liquid state at room temperature; it is a dark, reddish-brown, fuming, highly volatile and corrosive liquid. (ब्रोमीन — कमरे के तापमान पर द्रव अवस्था में पाई जाने वाली एकमात्र अधातु)

 

• It belongs to the halogen family (Group 17) of the periodic table, along with fluorine, chlorine, iodine and astatine.

 

• Bromine is used in making flame retardants, in photography (silver bromide), and in water purification.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option C.

 

Additional Information

 

• Among metals, mercury (Hg) is the only one that is liquid at room temperature.

 

• Nitrogen exists as a diatomic gas (N₂) at room temperature and makes up about 78% of the atmosphere.

 

• Iodine and Phosphorus are both solids at room temperature; iodine sublimes to give violet vapours on heating, and phosphorus exists in allotropic forms (white and red phosphorus).

 

NOTE

 

• Nitrogen (Option A): A colourless, odourless gas at room temperature.

 

• Iodine (Option B): A shiny, greyish-black solid that sublimes on heating.

 

• Phosphorous (Option D): A solid non-metal, occurring mainly as white phosphorus (highly reactive, kept under water) and red phosphorus (less reactive).

question: What are the products formed when an acid reacts with a metal hydrogen carbonate?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Salt + Water + Carbon dioxide.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A metal hydrogen carbonate (bicarbonate) reacts with an acid to give a salt, water and carbon dioxide gas. (धातु बाइकार्बोनेट + अम्ल → लवण + जल + CO₂)

 

• General reaction: Metal hydrogen carbonate + Acid → Salt + Water + Carbon dioxide.

 

• Example: NaHCO₃ + HCl → NaCl + H₂O + CO₂↑. The evolved CO₂ gas turns lime water milky, which is the standard laboratory test to confirm carbon dioxide.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option D.

 

Additional Information

 

• A metal carbonate also reacts similarly with acid: Metal carbonate + Acid → Salt + Water + Carbon dioxide (e.g., Na₂CO₃ + 2HCl → 2NaCl + H₂O + CO₂).

 

• A metal reacting with a dilute acid gives Salt + Hydrogen gas (e.g., Zn + H₂SO₄ → ZnSO₄ + H₂↑) — the reaction described in Option B, but for a different reactant (metal, not metal hydrogen carbonate).

 

• An acid + base (neutralisation) reaction gives Salt + Water only, without any gas evolved.

 

NOTE

 

• Salt + Oxygen + Carbon (Option A): Not a valid reaction outcome; no such products are formed from acid–bicarbonate reactions.

 

• Salt + Hydrogen gas (Option B): This is the product when an acid reacts with an active metal, not a metal hydrogen carbonate.

 

• Base + Hydrogen gas (Option C): Incorrect; a base is never a product of an acid reacting with a bicarbonate.

question: A light is travelling from a denser medium A to a rarer medium B. What will be the unit of refractive index of medium B with respect to medium A?
solution_text:
The correct answer is No unit.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The refractive index of one medium with respect to another is defined as the ratio of the speed of light in the first medium to the speed of light in the second medium (or equivalently, ratio of sine of angle of incidence to sine of angle of refraction). (अपवर्तनांक — एक अनुपात, इसलिए मात्रकहीन)

 

• Since refractive index is a ratio of two quantities having the same units (both are speeds, in m/s), the units cancel out completely.

 

• Therefore, refractive index is a dimensionless, pure number, and it has no unit, regardless of which pair of media is being compared.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option A.

 

Additional Information

 

• Refractive index of medium B with respect to A is written as ₐn_B = speed of light in A / speed of light in B.

 

• Absolute refractive index of a medium is its refractive index with respect to vacuum (or air), and for glass it is about 1.5, for water about 1.33, and for diamond about 2.42.

 

• A denser medium has a higher refractive index and a lower speed of light compared to a rarer medium.

 

NOTE

 

• (metre)⁻¹ (Option B): This would be the unit of a quantity like power of a lens (measured in dioptres), not refractive index.

 

• metre (Option C): A unit of length/distance, not applicable to a ratio like refractive index.

 

• (metre)² (Option D): A unit of area, again not relevant to a dimensionless ratio.

question: Which of the following statements correctly explains the continuous movement of particles of matter?
option_1: Particles of matter are too heavy to move.
option_2: Particles of matter are continuously moving due to their kinetic energy.
option_3: Particles of matter are stationary unless force is applied.
option_4: Particles of matter move only in gases and not in solids or liquids.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Particles of matter are continuously moving due to their kinetic energy.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• All matter is made up of tiny particles that possess kinetic energy, which keeps them in a state of continuous, random motion — this is one of the fundamental postulates of the kinetic theory of matter. (गतिज सिद्धांत — कणों में निरंतर गति उनकी गतिज ऊर्जा के कारण)

 

• This motion is present in all three states of matter — solids, liquids and gases — though the extent of motion is greatest in gases (particles move freely and rapidly), moderate in liquids, and least in solids (particles only vibrate about their fixed positions).

 

• The particle kinetic energy also increases with temperature, which is why processes like diffusion happen faster when a substance is heated.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option B.

 

Additional Information

 

• Diffusion — the intermixing of particles of two different substances on their own — is direct evidence of the continuous, random motion of particles.

 

• The Brownian motion of pollen grains suspended in water, discovered by Robert Brown, provided early experimental evidence for particle motion.

 

• The three states of matter (solid, liquid, gas) differ mainly in the space between particles, the force of attraction between them, and their kinetic energy.

 

NOTE

 

• Too heavy to move (Option A): Incorrect — particles of matter, even of a heavy substance, are always in motion due to kinetic energy.

 

• Stationary unless force applied (Option C): Incorrect — particle motion is intrinsic and continuous, not something that needs an external force to start.

 

• Only in gases (Option D): Incorrect — particles move in solids and liquids too, just to a much lesser extent than in gases.

question: Which of the following statements is NOT correct?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Loudness depends on frequency.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Loudness of a sound is a measure of how loud or soft it sounds to the ear, and it depends on the amplitude of the sound wave — larger the amplitude, louder the sound; smaller the amplitude, softer the sound. (प्रबलता — आयाम पर निर्भर, आवृत्ति पर नहीं)

 

• Frequency, on the other hand, determines the pitch (shrillness) of a sound, not its loudness — a high frequency gives a shrill/high-pitched sound, while low frequency gives a flat/deep sound, regardless of how loud or soft it is.

 

• Hence, the statement 'loudness depends on frequency' is factually incorrect, since loudness is governed by amplitude, and frequency governs pitch.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option D.

 

Additional Information

 

• Amplitude is the maximum displacement of particles of the medium from their mean position; it is measured in decibels (dB) when expressing loudness.

 

• Pitch (shrillness/flatness) depends on frequency, measured in hertz (Hz) — the number of complete oscillations per second.

 

• Quality (timbre) of sound helps distinguish two sounds of the same pitch and loudness (e.g., the same note played on a guitar vs a flute).

 

NOTE

 

• Loudness depends on amplitude (Option A): This is a correct statement, so it is NOT the answer.

 

• Soft sound has small amplitude (Option B): Correct — smaller amplitude means softer sound.

 

• Loud sound has large amplitude (Option C): Correct — larger amplitude means louder sound.

question: The potential energy of a body depends on which of the following?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both mass and height.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Gravitational potential energy of a body is given by the formula P.E. = mgh, where m is the mass of the body, g is the acceleration due to gravity, and h is the height above the reference level. (स्थितिज ऊर्जा — द्रव्यमान व ऊँचाई दोनों पर निर्भर)

 

• Since the formula involves both m and h as direct multiplying factors, the potential energy of a body depends on both its mass and its height — increasing either one increases the potential energy.

 

• Potential energy does not depend on the speed of the body — speed is instead linked to kinetic energy (K.E. = ½mv²).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option D.

 

Additional Information

 

• The SI unit of energy (both potential and kinetic) is the joule (J).

 

• Elastic potential energy is the energy stored in a stretched or compressed spring, and depends on the spring constant and the extent of deformation.

 

• The law of conservation of energy states that energy can neither be created nor destroyed, only transformed — e.g., potential energy converts to kinetic energy as a body falls.

 

NOTE

 

• Speed (Option A): Relevant to kinetic energy, not potential energy.

 

• Mass only (Option B): Incomplete — height is equally essential in the formula P.E. = mgh.

 

• Height only (Option C): Incomplete — mass is equally essential; a heavier body at the same height has more potential energy.

question: A car driver uses a concave mirror as a shaving mirror at home. If his face is kept close to the mirror, how will the image formed be?
option_1: Real, inverted, and smaller than the face
option_2: Real, inverted, and larger than the face
solution_text:
The correct answer is Virtual, erect, and magnified.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A concave mirror forms a virtual, erect and magnified image of an object when the object is placed very close to the mirror, i.e., between the pole and the focus (or within the focal length). (अवतल दर्पण — वस्तु फोकस के भीतर होने पर आभासी, सीधा, बड़ा प्रतिबिंब)

 

• This is exactly why concave mirrors are used as shaving mirrors, make-up mirrors and by dentists — the face (or tooth) is held close, well within the focal length, so a magnified, easy-to-see, upright image is obtained.

 

• As the object (face) is moved farther away from the mirror — beyond the focus — the concave mirror instead forms real, inverted images, which can be smaller, equal, or larger than the object depending on the exact distance.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option D.

 

Additional Information

 

• A concave mirror is a converging mirror, since it converges parallel rays of light to a real focus in front of it.

 

• Other everyday uses of concave mirrors: headlights of vehicles, torches, and solar cookers (to converge light/heat at a point), and as reflectors in reflecting telescopes.

 

• A convex mirror, by contrast, always forms a virtual, erect and diminished image, regardless of the object's distance — used in vehicle rear-view mirrors and security mirrors for a wider field of view.

 

NOTE

 

• Real, inverted and smaller than the face (Option A): Happens with a concave mirror only when the object is placed beyond the centre of curvature, far from the mirror.

 

• Real, inverted and larger than the face (Option B): Happens when the object is placed between focus and centre of curvature, again farther than the shaving-mirror scenario.

 

• Virtual, erect and diminished (Option C): This describes a convex mirror's image, not a concave mirror held close to the face.

question: A train is moving along a straight track with a speed of 54 km/hr. It stops after traveling 150 m. The magnitude of its acceleration is:
solution_text:
The correct answer is 0.75 m/s².

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Convert speed to m/s: u = 54 km/hr = 54 × 5/18 = 15 m/s. Final velocity v = 0 (train stops), and distance s = 150 m. (त्वरण = वेग में परिवर्तन की दर)

 

• Using the third equation of motion, v² = u² − 2as (deceleration, so negative sign):

 

• 0² = 15² − 2 × a × 150 ⇒ 0 = 225 − 300a ⇒ a = 225/300 = 0.75 m/s².

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option B.

 

Additional Information

 

• Since the train is slowing down, this is technically a retardation (deceleration) of magnitude 0.75 m/s², but the question only asks for the magnitude of acceleration.

 

• The conversion factor 1 km/hr = 5/18 m/s (and 1 m/s = 18/5 km/hr) is essential for such motion problems.

 

• The three equations of motion for uniform acceleration are: v = u + at, s = ut + ½at², and v² = u² + 2as.

 

NOTE

 

• Always convert speed to consistent SI units (m/s and metres) before applying the equations of motion, and remember to use a negative sign for deceleration when the object is stopping.

question: Which of the following metals is most likely to be found in the free state in nature due to its low reactivity?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gold.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Metals at the bottom of the reactivity series — such as gold, silver and platinum — are very unreactive (noble metals) and hence are found in nature in their free (native) elemental state, not combined with other elements. (सक्रियता श्रेणी में निम्नतम धातुएँ — प्रकृति में मुक्त अवस्था में)

 

• Gold does not readily react with oxygen, water or most acids, so it does not get oxidised or corroded in nature, and is found as native gold in rocks and river sands.

 

• Highly reactive metals, in contrast, are never found free in nature — they are always found as compounds (ores), e.g., oxides, sulphides or carbonates, because they readily combine with oxygen and moisture.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option A.

 

Additional Information

 

• The reactivity series (most to least reactive): K, Na, Ca, Mg, Al, Zn, Fe, Pb, (H), Cu, Hg, Ag, Au (roughly).

 

• Metals like Cu, Ag, Au occur in free state or as easily reducible compounds, while highly reactive metals like K, Na, Ca, Mg, Al are extracted using electrolytic reduction of their molten ores.

 

• Metals in the middle of the series (Zn, Fe, Pb, Cu) are usually extracted by reduction with carbon (Roasting/Calcination + Reduction).

 

NOTE

 

• Copper (Option B): Moderately reactive; mostly found combined as ores (e.g., copper pyrites), only occasionally in small native deposits.

 

• Zinc (Option C): Fairly reactive; always found combined in nature, chiefly as zinc blende (ZnS) and calamine (ZnCO₃).

 

• Iron (Option D): Reactive enough to rust readily in moist air; found combined as ores such as haematite and magnetite, never free.

question: Which of the following is secreted directly into the blood and carried to different parts of the body?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Adrenaline.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Adrenaline (epinephrine) is a hormone secreted by the adrenal glands (endocrine gland), and like all hormones, it is secreted directly into the bloodstream, which carries it to target organs throughout the body. (एड्रेनालिन — अंतःस्रावी ग्रंथि से सीधे रक्त में स्रावित हार्मोन)

 

• It is often called the 'fight or flight' hormone, released during stress, fear or excitement — it increases heart rate, blood pressure, and blood flow to muscles, preparing the body for immediate action.

 

• Saliva, pancreatic juice and bile juice are all exocrine secretions — they are released through ducts into the digestive tract (mouth/small intestine), not directly into the blood.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option D.

 

Additional Information

 

• Endocrine glands (ductless glands) release hormones directly into blood, e.g., pituitary, thyroid, adrenal, pancreas (islets of Langerhans).

 

• Exocrine glands release their secretions through ducts, e.g., salivary glands, liver (bile), pancreas (digestive enzymes), sweat and sebaceous glands.

 

• Interestingly, the pancreas is both an endocrine gland (secreting insulin and glucagon directly into blood) and an exocrine gland (secreting pancreatic juice via a duct into the duodenum).

 

NOTE

 

• Saliva (Option A): Secreted by salivary glands through ducts into the mouth; helps in digestion of starch.

 

• Pancreatic juice (Option B): Secreted by the exocrine part of the pancreas through the pancreatic duct into the duodenum.

 

• Bile juice (Option C): Produced by the liver, stored in the gallbladder, and released through the bile duct into the duodenum to aid fat digestion.

question: Which of the following is the common name for ethanol (C2H5OH)?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ethyl alcohol.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Ethanol (C₂H₅OH) is commonly known as ethyl alcohol, and in everyday language simply as 'alcohol' — it is the type of alcohol present in alcoholic beverages. (एथेनॉल — सामान्य भाषा में एथिल एल्कोहॉल)

 

• It is produced commercially by the fermentation of sugars (from molasses, grains, etc.) using yeast, and is also manufactured industrially from ethene.

 

• Ethanol has wide uses: as a solvent, in the preparation of tinctures and syrups, as fuel (ethanol blending in petrol), and as a key ingredient in sanitisers.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option D.

 

Additional Information

 

• Methanol (CH₃OH), or methyl alcohol, is a highly toxic alcohol used as an industrial solvent and fuel — drinking it can cause blindness or death.

 

• Ethanol reacts with sodium metal to liberate hydrogen gas, and with hot concentrated sulphuric acid to form ethene (dehydration reaction).

 

• A denatured alcohol is ethanol made unfit for drinking by adding poisonous substances like methanol or pyridine, so it can be sold for industrial use without alcohol tax.

 

NOTE

 

• Isopropyl alcohol (Option A): A different alcohol (propan-2-ol), commonly used in rubbing alcohol/antiseptics, not ethanol.

 

• Methyl alcohol (Option B): This is the common name of methanol (CH₃OH), a smaller and more toxic alcohol molecule.

 

• Butyl alcohol (Option C): The common name for butanol, a four-carbon alcohol, chemically distinct from ethanol.

question: Which of the following features is seen in every cell under a microscope?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Cell membrane.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The cell membrane (plasma membrane) is the basic, universal boundary that encloses the cytoplasm and contents of every living cell, whether plant, animal, or microbial, and is always visible around a cell under the microscope. (कोशिका झिल्ली — प्रत्येक कोशिका में उपस्थित)

 

• It is a thin, flexible, selectively permeable membrane composed mainly of a lipid bilayer with embedded proteins, and it regulates the entry and exit of substances into and out of the cell.

 

• Structures such as mitochondria, lysosomes and a defined chromosome/nucleus are not universally present in the same way — e.g., mature red blood cells lack a nucleus, and simple prokaryotic cells (bacteria) lack membrane-bound organelles like mitochondria and lysosomes.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option C.

 

Additional Information

 

• The cell membrane was described using the fluid mosaic model, proposed by Singer and Nicolson (1972).

 

• The cell theory (Schleiden, Schwann, and later Virchow) states that all living organisms are made of cells, and the cell is the basic structural and functional unit of life.

 

• Cells lacking a well-defined nucleus and membrane-bound organelles (e.g., bacteria) are called prokaryotic cells; cells with a true nucleus are eukaryotic cells.

 

NOTE

 

• Lysosome (Option A): A membrane-bound organelle found mainly in animal cells; absent in mature red blood cells and in many plant cells.

 

• Mitochondria (Option B): Present in most eukaryotic cells, but absent in prokaryotic cells (bacteria) and in mature mammalian red blood cells.

 

• Chromosome (Option D): Present as genetic material in all cells, but it is not always visible as a distinct, condensed structure — it is only seen as compact chromosomes during cell division; otherwise it exists as diffused chromatin.

question: An object is thrown vertically upwards with velocity u. Under the influence of gravity, the acceleration:
option_1: becomes zero at the highest point
option_3: acts opposite to the direction of motion
option_4: acts in the direction of motion
solution_text:
The correct answer is acts opposite to the direction of motion.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• When an object is thrown vertically upwards, it moves against the pull of gravity, so the acceleration due to gravity (g) always acts downwards, which is opposite to the object's upward direction of motion. (गुरुत्वीय त्वरण सदैव नीचे की ओर कार्य करता है)

 

• Because the acceleration is opposite to the velocity, the object continuously slows down as it rises, until its velocity becomes zero at the highest point, and then it falls back down, now accelerating in the same direction as its (downward) motion.

 

• Importantly, the acceleration due to gravity, g ≈ 9.8 m/s², remains constant in magnitude and direction (always downward) throughout the entire motion, including at the highest point.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option C.

 

Additional Information

 

• At the highest point, the velocity is zero, but the acceleration is NOT zero — it is still g, directed downward. This is a commonly tested and often confused concept.

 

• Time taken to rise to the highest point equals the time taken to fall back to the starting point (for motion under gravity alone, ignoring air resistance), and is given by t = u/g.

 

• Maximum height reached is given by H = u²/2g.

 

NOTE

 

• Becomes zero at highest point (Option A): Incorrect — it is the velocity, not the acceleration, that becomes zero at the highest point.

 

• Increases the upward velocity (Option B): Incorrect — gravity acts to decrease the upward velocity during the ascent.

 

• Acts in the direction of motion (Option D): Incorrect during the ascent (upward motion); this is only true once the object begins to fall back down.

question: When the current in a circuit is doubled, keeping resistance constant, the power dissipated in the resistor becomes:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Four times.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Electrical power dissipated in a resistor is given by P = I²R, where I is the current and R is the resistance. (विद्युत शक्ति — धारा के वर्ग के समानुपाती)

 

• Power is directly proportional to the square of the current (when R is constant): P ∝ I².

 

• If the current is doubled (I → 2I), the new power becomes P' = (2I)²R = 4I²R = 4P, i.e., four times the original power.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option C.

 

Additional Information

 

• Power can also be expressed as P = VI = V²/R, useful when voltage is known instead of current.

 

• The SI unit of electric power is the watt (W), and commercial electrical energy is measured in kilowatt-hour (kWh), popularly called a 'unit'.

 

• This I²R relationship is also the basis of Joule's law of heating, since electrical energy dissipated as heat, H = I²Rt.

 

NOTE

 

• Half (Option A) and One-fourth (Option D) would apply if the current were halved, not doubled.

 

• Double (Option B) would be correct only if power were directly (linearly) proportional to current, but it is actually proportional to the square of current, giving four times, not double.

question: What is the primary advantage of cross-pollination over self-pollination?
option_1: Does not depend on pollinating agents for producing progeny
option_2: Produces progeny that is identical to parent
option_3: Requires less energy input for generating the progeny
option_4: Introduces genetic variations, which improves chances of survival in progeny
solution_text:
The correct answer is Introduces genetic variations, which improves chances of survival in progeny.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Cross-pollination is the transfer of pollen grains from the anther of one flower to the stigma of a flower on a genetically different plant of the same species, whereas self-pollination occurs within the same flower or plant. (परागण — विषम परागण से आनुवंशिक विविधता)

 

• Because cross-pollination combines genetic material from two different parent plants, it introduces greater genetic variation into the offspring, compared to self-pollination, which tends to produce genetically similar/identical offspring to the single parent.

 

• This genetic variation is biologically valuable because it improves the population's ability to adapt to changing environmental conditions, resist diseases and pests, and thereby improves the overall chances of survival of the species over generations.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option D.

 

Additional Information

 

• Cross-pollination is carried out with the help of pollinating agents, such as wind, water, insects (bees, butterflies) and birds — so it actually depends on such agents, unlike self-pollination.

 

• Flowers that undergo cross-pollination often have adaptations such as bright colours, fragrance and nectar to attract pollinators.

 

• Self-pollination ensures purity of characters and requires no external pollinating agent, but it reduces genetic diversity and can lead to accumulation of harmful recessive traits over generations (inbreeding depression).

 

NOTE

 

• Does not depend on pollinating agents (Option A): This is actually a feature of self-pollination, not cross-pollination — cross-pollination requires an external agent.

 

• Produces progeny identical to parent (Option B): This describes self-pollination (and asexual reproduction), not the outcome of cross-pollination.

 

• Requires less energy input (Option C): Self-pollination is generally the less energy/resource-intensive process, since it does not need to attract pollinators.

question: At maturity, an organism breaks into smaller pieces, which grow into new individuals. What is this process called?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Fragmentation.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Fragmentation is a type of asexual reproduction in which, on maturity, the body of a simple multicellular organism breaks up into two or more pieces (fragments), and each fragment then grows and develops into a complete new individual. (खंडन — जनक का टूटकर नए जीवों में विकसित होना)

 

• This mode of reproduction is commonly seen in simple organisms with a relatively simple body organisation, such as Spirogyra (a filamentous alga) and Hydra, where a chance breakage of the body into fragments leads to the formation of new organisms.

 

• The key feature that distinguishes fragmentation is that it happens at maturity, and the resulting individuals are genetically identical (clones) to the parent, since no fusion of gametes is involved.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option C.

 

Additional Information

 

• Binary fission is the division of a single-celled organism (e.g., Amoeba, bacteria) into two equal, genetically identical daughter cells.

 

• Budding is asexual reproduction where a small outgrowth called a bud develops on the parent body (e.g., Hydra, yeast) and eventually detaches to form a new individual — the parent body itself does not break apart.

 

• Regeneration is a related but distinct phenomenon, where a body part or a specific fragment can regrow the missing/entire organism, seen in organisms like Planaria.

 

NOTE

 

• Fusion (Option A): The joining together of two gametes (sexual reproduction), the opposite process of breaking apart.

 

• Budding (Option B): New individuals grow as outgrowths (buds) from the parent, without the parent's body breaking into fragments.

 

• Fission (Option D): Refers to a single-celled organism dividing into two (binary fission) or more (multiple fission) cells, not a multicellular organism breaking into fragments.

question: Which substances are selectively reabsorbed in the nephron?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Glucose, amino acids, and water.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In the nephron (the functional unit of the kidney), after filtration of blood occurs at the glomerulus to form the filtrate, useful substances such as glucose, amino acids, salts and most of the water are selectively reabsorbed back into the blood as the filtrate passes along the tubule (PCT, loop of Henle, DCT). (वृक्क नलिका में चयनात्मक पुनर्अवशोषण)

 

• This selective reabsorption ensures that useful nutrients and the required amount of water are conserved by the body, while unwanted waste products remain in the filtrate.

 

• Substances like urea, uric acid and excess water/salts, which are not reabsorbed, continue down the tubule and are eventually excreted as urine.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option B.

 

Additional Information

 

• The three main steps of urine formation are: Filtration (at Bowman's capsule/glomerulus), Selective Reabsorption (along the tubule), and Tubular Secretion (of substances like H⁺, K⁺, ammonia directly into the tubule).

 

• The nephron consists of the Malpighian corpuscle (glomerulus + Bowman's capsule) and a long tubule consisting of the proximal convoluted tubule, loop of Henle, and distal convoluted tubule, which opens into a collecting duct.

 

• Dialysis is an artificial process that performs the function of the kidney (removing wastes from blood) in patients with kidney failure.

 

NOTE

 

• Bile and hydrochloric acid (Option A): These are digestive secretions produced by the liver and stomach respectively; they are not related to the nephron's reabsorption function.

 

• Platelets and enzymes (Option C): Platelets are blood cells involved in clotting; being large cellular components, they are not even filtered at the glomerulus, let alone reabsorbed.

 

• Urea and carbon dioxide (Option D): Urea is a waste product that is deliberately excreted, not reabsorbed; carbon dioxide is removed mainly via the lungs, not the nephron.

question: Sohan purchased 25 dozens of toys at the rate of ₹480 per dozen. He sold each one of them at the rate of ₹45. What was his percentage profit?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. 12.5%.

 

GIVEN

 

• 25 dozens of toys bought at ₹480 per dozen; each toy sold at ₹45.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Cost price per toy = 480 ÷ 12 = ₹40.

 

• Selling price per toy = ₹45.

 

• Profit per toy = 45 − 40 = ₹5.

 

• Profit % = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100 = (5 ÷ 40) × 100 = 12.5%.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Profit% = (SP − CP)/CP × 100. Here SP = 45, CP = 40, difference = 5, and 5 is 1/8 of 40, so profit% = 1/8 × 100 = 12.5%.

 

NOTE

 

• Number of toys (25 dozens) is not needed — profit % is independent of total quantity, since it is a per-unit ratio. Note: this PDF prints all four options identically as 'X).5%' (with the leading digits missing); the number of dozens purchased (25) does not affect the profit percentage calculation.

question: Train P, going at the speed of 51 km/hr, completely passes Train Q of length 225 m, going in the same direction on parallel tracks, at 22 km/hr, in 7.5 minutes. How much time (in seconds) will P take to completely cross Train R of length 420 m, going at 21 km/hr in the opposite direction?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. 191.

 

GIVEN

 

• Speed of P = 51 km/hr; Train Q: length 225 m, speed 22 km/hr, same direction, P crosses Q in 7.5 minutes.

 

• Train R: length 420 m, speed 21 km/hr, opposite direction.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Step 1 (find length of P): Same direction ⇒ relative speed = 51 − 22 = 29 km/hr = 29 × 5/18 = 145/18 m/s.

 

• Time to cross Q = 7.5 minutes = 450 seconds. Distance covered = relative speed × time = (145/18) × 450 = 3625 m.

 

• This distance equals (length of P + length of Q): P + 225 = 3625 ⇒ P = 3400 m.

 

• Step 2 (cross R, opposite direction): relative speed = 51 + 21 = 72 km/hr = 72 × 5/18 = 20 m/s.

 

• Total distance to cross = length of P + length of R = 3400 + 420 = 3820 m.

 

• Time = distance ÷ speed = 3820 ÷ 20 = 191 seconds.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Always find the unknown train length first using: (relative speed) × (time) = sum of the two lengths, then reuse that length for the next crossing.

 

NOTE

 

• Same direction ⇒ relative speed = difference of speeds; opposite direction ⇒ relative speed = sum of speeds. Always convert km/hr to m/s using ×5/18 before working in metres and seconds.

question: If the mean proportional of A and 50 is 40, then find the value of A.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. 32.

 

GIVEN

 

• Mean proportional of A and 50 is 40.

 

SOLUTION

 

• If the mean proportional of two numbers x and y is m, then m² = x × y.

 

• Here, 40² = A × 50 ⇒ 1600 = 50A.

 

• A = 1600 ÷ 50 = 32.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Mean proportional of a and b = √(ab). So set (mean proportional)² = product of the two numbers, and solve directly for the unknown.

 

NOTE

 

• Do not confuse mean proportional (geometric mean, √(ab)) with the simple average (a+b)/2 — they are different concepts.

question: Simplify: 21³ + 13³ − 34³ + 3 × 21 × 13 × 34
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. 0.

 

GIVEN

 

• 21³ + 13³ − 34³ + 3 × 21 × 13 × 34.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Notice that 21 + 13 = 34. Let a = 21, b = 13, c = −34, so that a + b + c = 21 + 13 − 34 = 0.

 

• Identity: if a + b + c = 0, then a³ + b³ + c³ = 3abc.

 

• Here a³ + b³ + c³ = 21³ + 13³ + (−34)³ = 21³ + 13³ − 34³, and 3abc = 3 × 21 × 13 × (−34) = −(3 × 21 × 13 × 34).

 

• So 21³ + 13³ − 34³ = −(3 × 21 × 13 × 34).

 

• Adding 3 × 21 × 13 × 34 to both sides: 21³ + 13³ − 34³ + 3 × 21 × 13 × 34 = −(3×21×13×34) + 3×21×13×34 = 0.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Whenever you see three numbers where the third equals the sum of the other two (here 34 = 21 + 13) inside an a³+b³−c³ type expression along with a 3abc-style term, immediately apply a+b+c=0 ⇒ a³+b³+c³=3abc — it avoids all the heavy cubing.

 

NOTE

 

• Never attempt to actually cube 21, 13 and 34 directly — spotting the identity saves several minutes in the exam.

question: The sides of a triangle are 75 cm, 44 cm, and 35 cm. What is the length of its altitude corresponding to the side with a length of 44 cm?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. 21 cm.

 

GIVEN

 

• Sides of the triangle: 75 cm, 44 cm, 35 cm. Altitude required is on the side of length 44 cm (taken as base).

 

SOLUTION

 

• Semi-perimeter, s = (75 + 44 + 35) ÷ 2 = 154 ÷ 2 = 77 cm.

 

• By Heron's formula, Area = √[s(s−a)(s−b)(s−c)] = √[77 × (77−75) × (77−44) × (77−35)] = √[77 × 2 × 33 × 42].

 

• 77 × 2 = 154; 154 × 33 = 5082; 5082 × 42 = 213444. So Area = √213444 = 462 cm².

 

• Altitude on base 44 cm: Area = ½ × base × height ⇒ 462 = ½ × 44 × h ⇒ 462 = 22h ⇒ h = 462 ÷ 22 = 21 cm.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Altitude on a given side = (2 × Area) ÷ (that side). Once Area is found via Heron's formula, this single step gives the answer for any of the three altitudes.

 

NOTE

 

• s(s−a)(s−b)(s−c) values (77, 2, 33, 42) are worth factorising into perfect squares where possible to simplify the square root by hand: 213444 = 4 × 53361 = 4 × 231² gives √213444 = 2×231=462.

question: The areas of three adjacent faces of a solid cuboid are 108 cm², 60 cm² and 45 cm². What is the volume (in cm³) of the cuboid?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. 540.

 

GIVEN

 

• Areas of three adjacent faces of a cuboid: ab = 108 cm², bc = 60 cm², ca = 45 cm².

 

SOLUTION

 

• Multiply all three: (ab)(bc)(ca) = a²b²c² = (abc)² = 108 × 60 × 45.

 

• 108 × 60 = 6480; 6480 × 45 = 291600. So (abc)² = 291600.

 

• Volume = abc = √291600 = 540 cm³.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• For a cuboid, if the three face areas are p, q, r, then Volume = √(p × q × r) — a direct one-line formula, no need to separately find a, b, c.

 

NOTE

 

• Volume of a cuboid = length × breadth × height (abc); this trick works because multiplying the three face areas gives (abc)² directly.

question: A cistern is normally filled in 12 hours but takes 2 hours longer to fill because of a leak in its bottom. If the cistern is full, then in how much time will the leak empty the tank?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. 84 hours.

 

GIVEN

 

• Normal filling time (no leak) = 12 hours. With leak, filling takes 12 + 2 = 14 hours.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Rate of filling pipe alone = 1/12 (tank per hour).

 

• Net rate of filling with leak = 1/14 (tank per hour).

 

• Rate of leak (emptying) = (Filling rate) − (Net rate) = 1/12 − 1/14.

 

• LCM of 12,14 = 84: 1/12 = 7/84, 1/14 = 6/84. So leak rate = 7/84 − 6/84 = 1/84 tank per hour.

 

• So the leak alone would empty the full tank in 84 hours.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Leak's emptying time = (fill time with leak × fill time without leak) ÷ (difference in times) = (14 × 12) ÷ 2 = 168 ÷ 2 = 84 hours.

 

NOTE

 

• Always treat 'filling rate' as positive and 'leak/emptying rate' as negative when they act together; net rate = filling rate − leak rate.

question: Find the HCF of 27, 54 and 108.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. 27.

 

GIVEN

 

• Numbers: 27, 54 and 108.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Prime factorise: 27 = 3³; 54 = 2 × 3³; 108 = 2² × 3³.

 

• HCF = product of the lowest power of each common prime factor = 3³ = 27.

 

• (Check: 54 = 2 × 27, and 108 = 4 × 27, so both are exact multiples of 27, confirming HCF = 27.)

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• If the smallest number in the set exactly divides all the other numbers, then the smallest number itself is the HCF. Here 27 divides both 54 and 108 exactly.

 

NOTE

 

• Always check divisibility of the smallest number into the others first — it's the fastest way to spot the HCF without full factorisation.

question: In an election between two candidates, 20% of the total votes were declared invalid. The winning candidate received 70% of the valid votes and won by a margin of 12,400 votes. Find the total number of registered voters.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. 38,750.

 

GIVEN

 

• Invalid votes = 20% of total; winner got 70% of valid votes; winning margin = 12,400 votes.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Valid votes = 80% of total registered voters (assuming all registered voters cast a vote).

 

• Of the valid votes, winner = 70%, loser = 30% ⇒ margin = 70% − 30% = 40% of valid votes = 12,400.

 

• Valid votes = 12,400 ÷ 0.40 = 31,000.

 

• Total registered voters = Valid votes ÷ 80% = 31,000 ÷ 0.80 = 38,750.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Margin % (of valid votes) = (winner% − loser%). Valid votes = margin ÷ margin%. Total = valid votes ÷ (valid %  of total).

 

NOTE

 

• Do not confuse 'total votes/registered voters' (100%) with 'valid votes' (100% − invalid%) — the margin is always a percentage of valid votes, not of the total.

question: The angle of elevation of the top of a tree at a distance of 60 m from its foot on a horizontal plane is found to be 30°. Find the height of the tree.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. 20√3 m.

 

GIVEN

 

• Distance from foot of tree = 60 m; angle of elevation of top = 30°.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Let height of tree = h. In the right triangle, tan(30°) = height ÷ distance = h ÷ 60.

 

• tan(30°) = 1/√3, so h = 60 × (1/√3) = 60/√3.

 

• Rationalise: h = 60/√3 × (√3/√3) = 60√3/3 = 20√3 m.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Height = base × tan(angle of elevation). For 30°, tan = 1/√3, so Height = Base/√3, then rationalise by multiplying with √3/√3.

 

NOTE

 

• Standard trigonometric values to memorise: tan 30° = 1/√3, tan 45° = 1, tan 60° = √3.

question: Aman and Yogita together invested ₹59,200 in a business. At the end of the year, out of a total profit of ₹8,000, Aman's share was ₹1,400. How much was Aman's investment?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. ₹10,360.

 

GIVEN

 

• Total investment = ₹59,200; total profit = ₹8,000; Aman's share of profit = ₹1,400.

 

SOLUTION

 

• In a partnership (equal time period for both), profit share is directly proportional to investment: (Aman's investment)/(Total investment) = (Aman's profit)/(Total profit).

 

• Aman's investment = (Aman's profit ÷ Total profit) × Total investment = (1,400 ÷ 8,000) × 59,200.

 

• 1,400 ÷ 8,000 = 0.175. So Aman's investment = 0.175 × 59,200 = ₹10,360.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Since time is same for both partners, profit ratio = investment ratio directly. Just scale total investment by the fraction (individual profit ÷ total profit).

 

NOTE

 

• This shortcut (profit ratio = capital ratio) only applies when both partners invest for the same duration; if durations differ, use capital × time for each partner.

question: An Uber auto covers a distance of 680 km in 17 hours. What is its speed in km/hr?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. 40.

 

GIVEN

 

• Distance = 680 km; time = 17 hours.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Speed = Distance ÷ Time = 680 ÷ 17 = 40 km/hr.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• 17 × 40 = 680; recognising that 17 × 4 = 68 makes the mental division instant.

 

NOTE

 

• Speed = Distance/Time is the most basic motion formula; always keep units consistent (km with hours gives km/hr).

question: The value of (0.896 × 0.763 + 0.896 × 0.237) ÷ (0.7 × 0.064 + 0.7 × 0.936) is:
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. 1.28.

 

GIVEN

 

• Expression: (0.896 × 0.763 + 0.896 × 0.237) ÷ (0.7 × 0.064 + 0.7 × 0.936).

 

SOLUTION

 

• Take 0.896 common in the numerator: 0.896 × (0.763 + 0.237) = 0.896 × 1 = 0.896.

 

• Take 0.7 common in the denominator: 0.7 × (0.064 + 0.936) = 0.7 × 1 = 0.7.

 

• Value = 0.896 ÷ 0.7 = 1.28.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Whenever a sum/difference in brackets has a common multiplying factor on both terms, factor it out first — here the two decimal pairs (0.763+0.237) and (0.064+0.936) are each designed to add up to exactly 1, making the whole expression collapse to a simple division.

 

NOTE

 

• Always scan for numbers that sum to a round value like 1 or 10 in a×b + a×c style expressions — it's a strong hint to factor rather than multiply out.

question: A credit card payment that will settle a bill for 383 mixers at ₹1,000 per mixer with successive discounts of 25% and 20% with a further discount of 13% on card payment is:
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. ₹1,99,926.

 

GIVEN

 

• 383 mixers at ₹1,000 each; successive discounts of 25%, then 20%, then a further 13% for card payment.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Total marked price = 383 × 1,000 = ₹3,83,000.

 

• After 25% discount: 3,83,000 × 0.75 = ₹2,87,250.

 

• After further 20% discount: 2,87,250 × 0.80 = ₹2,29,800.

 

• After further 13% card discount: 2,29,800 × 0.87 = ₹1,99,926.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• For successive discounts, multiply the base price by (1 − d₁)(1 − d₂)(1 − d₃) in one go: 3,83,000 × 0.75 × 0.80 × 0.87 = 1,99,926, rather than converting each stage to an equivalent single discount %.

 

NOTE

 

• Successive discounts are NEVER simply added (25%+20%+13% ≠ 58% off) — each discount applies to the already-reduced price, so they must be multiplied as successive factors.

question: Simplify 3 x 5 + 8 − 15 ÷ 3 − 12 + 72 ÷ 8 x 5 − 32.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. 19.

 

GIVEN

 

• 3 × 5 + 8 − 15 ÷ 3 − 12 + 72 ÷ 8 × 5 − 32.

 

SOLUTION (BODMAS: Division/Multiplication before Addition/Subtraction, left to right)

 

• 3 × 5 = 15.

 

• 15 ÷ 3 = 5.

 

• 72 ÷ 8 × 5 (left to right): 72 ÷ 8 = 9, then 9 × 5 = 45.

 

• Substitute back: 15 + 8 − 5 − 12 + 45 − 32.

 

• Left to right: 15+8=23; 23−5=18; 18−12=6; 6+45=51; 51−32=19.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Group all resulting positive terms and negative terms separately: Positives = 15+8+45=68; Negatives = 5+12+32=49; 68 − 49 = 19.

 

NOTE

 

• Always fully resolve every ×/÷ operation (left to right, same precedence) before doing any +/− — a common mistake is doing + and − before finishing all multiplication/division.

question: Consider two triangles, ABC and XYZ. In triangle ABC, the base is 21 cm and the other two sides are 17 cm and 10 cm, respectively. In triangle XYZ, the base is two-thirds the base of triangle ABC and has an altitude of 5 cm. Find the sum of the areas of triangles ABC and XYZ.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. 119 cm².

 

GIVEN

 

• Triangle ABC: sides 21 cm, 17 cm, 10 cm. Triangle XYZ: base = (2/3) × 21 cm, altitude = 5 cm.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Area of ABC by Heron's formula: s = (21+17+10)/2 = 48/2 = 24.

 

• Area = √[s(s−a)(s−b)(s−c)] = √[24 × (24−21) × (24−17) × (24−10)] = √[24 × 3 × 7 × 14].

 

• 24 × 3 = 72; 72 × 7 = 504; 504 × 14 = 7056. √7056 = 84 cm².

 

• Base of XYZ = (2/3) × 21 = 14 cm; altitude = 5 cm.

 

• Area of XYZ = ½ × base × height = ½ × 14 × 5 = 35 cm².

 

• Sum of areas = 84 + 35 = 119 cm².

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Recognise 21-17-10 doesn't form a standard triplet, so Heron's formula is unavoidable; but always check if s and (s−a),(s−b),(s−c) multiply to a perfect square to simplify the square root quickly (7056 = 84²).

 

NOTE

 

• Don't confuse 'base' of the second triangle with its full side lengths — only base and height are needed for a direct ½×b×h area, no need for Heron's formula there.

question: A certain sum of money amounts to ₹7,040 in 2 years and ₹8,000 in 5 years on simple interest. Find the principal.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. ₹6,400.

 

GIVEN

 

• Amount after 2 years = ₹7,040; Amount after 5 years = ₹8,000 (simple interest).

 

SOLUTION

 

• Since SI is uniform per year, the increase from year 2 to year 5 (3 years) = 8,000 − 7,040 = ₹960.

 

• SI per year = 960 ÷ 3 = ₹320.

 

• SI for 2 years = 320 × 2 = ₹640.

 

• Principal = Amount after 2 years − SI for 2 years = 7,040 − 640 = ₹6,400.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Find annual SI from the difference in amounts over the difference in years; then Principal = (any amount) − (SI up to that time).

 

NOTE

 

• In simple interest problems, the amount grows by a constant amount each year — always exploit this linearity to find the annual interest directly.

question: Manoj got a new curtain at 20% discount. If Manoj did not get any discount, Manoj would have to pay ₹664 extra. So how much did Manoj pay for the curtain?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. ₹2,656.

 

GIVEN

 

• Discount = 20% of marked price; the discount amount itself = ₹664 (the 'extra' he would have paid without the discount).

 

SOLUTION

 

• 20% of Marked Price (MP) = ₹664 ⇒ MP = 664 ÷ 0.20 = ₹3,320.

 

• Amount actually paid = MP − Discount = 3,320 − 664 = ₹2,656.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• 'Extra amount without discount' = the discount amount itself. So MP = (extra amount) ÷ (discount %), and Amount Paid = MP − extra amount, or directly MP × (1 − discount%).

 

NOTE

 

• Amount paid = MP × 0.80 = 3,320 × 0.80 = 2,656 — a quick cross-check using the complementary percentage (100% − 20% = 80%).

question: A, B, and C can do a piece of work in 3, 3, and 3 days respectively. How long (in days) will they take to do thrice the same work, working together?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. 3.

 

GIVEN

 

• A, B and C each alone can finish the (same) piece of work in 3 days.

 

SOLUTION

 

• A's 1-day work = 1/3; B's 1-day work = 1/3; C's 1-day work = 1/3.

 

• Combined 1-day work = 1/3 + 1/3 + 1/3 = 1 (i.e., the whole work is done in exactly 1 day working together).

 

• Time to complete thrice (3×) the work together = 3 × 1 day = 3 days.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• If three people each alone take the same n days, together they take n/3 days for 1 work; for k times the work, time = k × n/3. Here n=3,k=3 ⇒ time = 3×3/3 = 3 days.

 

NOTE

 

• Always convert 'time to complete' into 'work done per day' (rate) — rates add up directly when people work together, times do not.

question: The product of the present ages of Seema and Jyoti is 3,952 years, and their present age ratio is 19 : 13. Find the difference in the ages (in years) of Seema and Jyoti.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. 24.

 

GIVEN

 

• Product of ages = 3,952; ratio of ages = 19 : 13.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Let ages be 19x and 13x. Product: 19x × 13x = 247x² = 3,952.

 

• x² = 3,952 ÷ 247 = 16 ⇒ x = √16 = 4.

 

• Seema's age = 19 × 4 = 76 years; Jyoti's age = 13 × 4 = 52 years.

 

• Difference = 76 − 52 = 24 years.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Difference in ages = (difference of ratio terms) × x = (19−13) × x = 6 × 4 = 24, without separately computing both ages.

 

NOTE

 

• Whenever a ratio and a product are given, express both quantities as (ratio term)×x, multiply to get x², then take the square root — this is the standard 'ratio-product' technique.

question: The income of Raman is ₹70,900. He saves 12% of his income. If his income increases by 39% and expenditure increases by 50%, then his savings will:
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. decrease by ₹3,545.

 

GIVEN

 

• Income = ₹70,900; savings = 12% of income; income increases by 39%; expenditure increases by 50%.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Original savings = 12% of 70,900 = ₹8,508.

 

• Original expenditure = 88% of 70,900 = ₹62,392.

 

• New income = 70,900 × 1.39 = ₹98,551.

 

• New expenditure = 62,392 × 1.50 = ₹93,588.

 

• New savings = New income − New expenditure = 98,551 − 93,588 = ₹4,963.

 

• Change in savings = 4,963 − 8,508 = −₹3,545, i.e. a decrease of ₹3,545.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Always compute expenditure = Income − Savings first, then scale income and expenditure separately by their own growth percentages before subtracting again for new savings.

 

NOTE

 

• A common mistake is applying the income growth % to savings directly — savings must always be recomputed as (new income − new expenditure), not scaled directly.

question: The sum of seven consecutive numbers is 168. What is the sum of the largest and smallest numbers?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. 48.

 

GIVEN

 

• Sum of 7 consecutive numbers = 168.

 

SOLUTION

 

• For 7 consecutive numbers, the middle (4th) number is the average: middle number = 168 ÷ 7 = 24.

 

• The seven numbers are 21, 22, 23, 24, 25, 26, 27 (three below and three above 24).

 

• Smallest = 21, Largest = 27. Sum of largest and smallest = 21 + 27 = 48.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• In any set of consecutive numbers (odd count), sum ÷ count = middle term. Also, (smallest + largest) = 2 × middle term = 2 × 24 = 48 directly, since they are equidistant from the middle.

 

NOTE

 

• For consecutive numbers arranged symmetrically, smallest + largest always equals 2 × the middle (average) term — no need to list all seven numbers.

question: 1/20 is what percentage of 11/40 (rounded off to two decimal places)?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. 18.18%.

 

GIVEN

 

• Find what percentage 1/20 is of 11/40.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Required % = (1/20) ÷ (11/40) × 100 = (1/20) × (40/11) × 100.

 

• (1/20) × (40/11) = 40/220 = 2/11.

 

• (2/11) × 100 = 200/11 = 18.1818...% ≈ 18.18%.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• 'A is what % of B' = (A/B) × 100. Converting the fraction division to multiplication by the reciprocal (×40/11) is the fastest route here.

 

NOTE

 

• 2/11 is a well-known recurring decimal (0.1818...); memorising common fraction-to-percentage conversions like this speeds up such questions.

question: The average age of 50 students in a class is 29 years. If the age of the teacher is also included, the average of the whole group becomes 30 years. The age (in years) of the teacher is:
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. 80.

 

GIVEN

 

• Average age of 50 students = 29 years; average of 51 people (including teacher) = 30 years.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Sum of ages of 50 students = 50 × 29 = 1,450.

 

• Sum of ages of 51 people (including teacher) = 51 × 30 = 1,530.

 

• Teacher's age = 1,530 − 1,450 = 80 years.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• New person's value = New total sum − Old total sum. Or: Teacher's age = old average + (number of students × increase in average) = 29 + (50 × 1) = 79+...  — more reliably, use sums directly as shown above to avoid sign errors.

 

NOTE

 

• When one new member joins and raises the average, the new member's value is always greater than the new average; here 80 > 30, which makes sense since it single-handedly pulled up the average of 50 people.

question: The average of the first 5 odd natural numbers is:
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. 5.

 

GIVEN

 

• First 5 odd natural numbers: 1, 3, 5, 7, 9.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Sum = 1 + 3 + 5 + 7 + 9 = 25.

 

• Average = Sum ÷ Count = 25 ÷ 5 = 5.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• The average of the first n odd natural numbers is always equal to n itself (since they are symmetric around the middle term). Here n = 5, so average = 5 directly, without adding.

 

NOTE

 

• Compare: average of first n natural numbers = (n+1)/2, while average of first n odd natural numbers = n — these are commonly confused, so remember them separately.

question:
Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

Statements: All shirts are trousers. All trousers are pants. No pant is a coat.

Conclusion (I) : No shirt is a coat.

Conclusion (II) : No trouser is a coat.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. Both conclusions follow.

 

GIVEN

 

• Statements: All shirts are trousers; All trousers are pants; No pant is a coat.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Chain the statements: Shirts ⊆ Trousers ⊆ Pants, and Pants ∩ Coats = ∅ (no pant is a coat).

 

• Since Trousers ⊆ Pants, and no pant is a coat, it follows that no trouser is a coat → Conclusion II follows.

 

• Since Shirts ⊆ Trousers ⊆ Pants, and no pant is a coat, it also follows that no shirt is a coat → Conclusion I follows.

 

• Both conclusions are valid logical consequences of the chain of statements.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Draw nested circles: Shirt inside Trouser inside Pant, with Coat as a completely separate circle outside Pant. Any group fully inside Pant is automatically excluded from Coat — this instantly confirms both conclusions.

 

NOTE

 

• In syllogism, always chain 'All A are B, All B are C' into 'All A are C' before checking conclusions — most 3-statement syllogisms reduce to a simple chain like this one.

question:
This question is based on the five, three-digit numbers given below.

(Left) 551 214 483 409 581 (Right)

(Example- 697 – First digit = 6, second digit = 9 and third digit = 7)

(NOTE - All operations to be done from left to right.)

What will be the resultant if the second digit of the highest number is added to the third digit of the lowest number?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. 12.

 

GIVEN

 

• Numbers: 551, 214, 483, 409, 581.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Highest number among these = 581. Its second digit = 8.

 

• Lowest number among these = 214. Its third digit = 4.

 

• Resultant = 8 + 4 = 12.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• First scan just the hundreds digit of each number to instantly rank them (5,2,4,4,5 → 581 & 551 are the two largest, 214 is clearly smallest), then only extract the specific digits asked for.

 

NOTE

 

• Always double check 'digit position' counting starts from the left (first digit = hundreds place) as defined by the example given in the question.

question:
If 'A' stands for '÷', 'B' stands for '×', 'C' stands for '+' and 'D' stands for '–', what will come in place of the question mark (?) in the following equation?

6 C 8 B 8 A 32 D 1 = ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. 7.

 

GIVEN

 

• A = ÷, B = ×, C = +, D = −. Equation: 6 C 8 B 8 A 32 D 1.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Replace letters with their symbols: 6 + 8 × 8 ÷ 32 − 1.

 

• Apply BODMAS: 8 × 8 = 64; 64 ÷ 32 = 2.

 

• Now: 6 + 2 − 1 = 8 − 1 = 7.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Substitute the letters first, then solve purely with BODMAS as a normal numeric expression — do all × and ÷ (left to right) before + and −.

 

NOTE

 

• A common mistake is solving left to right ignoring operator precedence; always finish multiplication/division first even in letter-coded equations.

question:
A, B, C, D, E, F and G are sitting around a circular table facing the centre. D is the immediate neighbour of G and A. F sits second to the left of G. E is the immediate neighbour of C and A.

How many people sit between C and B when counted from the left of B?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. One.

 

GIVEN

 

• 7 people (A,B,C,D,E,F,G) around a circular table facing centre; D is between G & A; F is second to the left of G; E is between C & A.

 

SOLUTION

 

• D is the immediate neighbour of both G and A, so the trio G–D–A sit consecutively.

 

• E is the immediate neighbour of both C and A, so C–E–A sit consecutively; combined with the above, A's two neighbours are D and E, giving the block: G–D–A–E–C.

 

• Place G, D, A, E, C at positions 1,2,3,4,5 (clockwise); positions 6,7 remain for B and F.

 

• 'F sits second to the left of G' (left = clockwise direction): G is at 1, so 2 steps clockwise = position 3 — but that's taken by A. So instead the G–D–A–E–C block must run anticlockwise from G, giving G=1, D=7, A=6, E=5, C=4, leaving positions 2,3 for B and F.

 

• Second to the left of G(1) = position 3 ⇒ F = 3, so B = 2.

 

• Final arrangement (clockwise): 1=G, 2=B, 3=F, 4=C, 5=E, 6=A, 7=D.

 

• From B (position 2), moving left (clockwise): next is F(3), then C(4). So only F sits between B and C — that is One person.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• When two different people are both stated to be immediate neighbours of the same person (here A, neighboured by both D and E), that person's two seats are automatically fixed — build the block first, then fit remaining clues around it.

 

NOTE

 

• Remember the standard convention: for people facing the centre of a round table with seats labelled clockwise, moving to a person's 'left' corresponds to moving clockwise, and 'right' corresponds to moving anticlockwise.

question:
A group of numbers/symbols is coded using letter codes as per the codes given below and the conditions that follow. Note: If none of the conditions apply, then the codes for the respective number/symbol are to be followed directly as given in the table.

Numbers/symbols: % 8 2 $ 9 3 & 7 @ 6 + 5 # 4

Codes: T P G R W S C N L J H K A Y

Conditions:

(i) If the first element is a symbol and the last element a number, the codes for these two (the first and last elements) are to be interchanged.

(ii) If both the second and third elements are multiples of 2, the third element is to be coded as the code for the second element.

(iii) If the second element is an odd number and the last element is a symbol, the second and last elements are to be coded as *.

What will be the code for the following group?

& 4 8 $ #
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. C Y Y R A.

 

GIVEN

 

• Codes: % =T, 8=P, 2=G, $=R, 9=W, 3=S, &=C, 7=N, @=L, 6=J, +=H, 5=K, #=A, 4=Y. Group: & 4 8 $ #.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Elements: 1st=& (symbol), 2nd=4 (number), 3rd=8 (number), 4th=$ (symbol), 5th (last)=# (symbol).

 

• Check condition (i): first is a symbol, but last (#) is a symbol, NOT a number — condition does not apply.

 

• Check condition (ii): 2nd = 4 (even, multiple of 2) and 3rd = 8 (even, multiple of 2) — both are multiples of 2, so condition applies: the 3rd element is coded as the code of the 2nd element.

 

• Base codes: & → C, 4 → Y, 8 → P, $ → R, # → A.

 

• Apply condition (ii): 3rd element (8) is recoded to the code of the 2nd element (4), i.e., Y instead of P.

 

• Check condition (iii): 2nd element (4) is even, not odd — condition does not apply.

 

• Final codes in order: C, Y, Y, R, A → C Y Y R A.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Always check the conditions strictly in order and verify the exact trigger (symbol/number, odd/even) for each position before coding — apply only the conditions whose exact criteria are met, and code everything else directly from the table.

 

NOTE

 

• Condition (ii) does not swap the 2nd and 3rd codes — it specifically overwrites only the 3rd element's code with the 2nd element's code, so the 2nd element keeps its own original code.

question:
Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

Statements:

Some cakes are samosas.

All samosas are buns.

Conclusions:

(I): Some cakes are buns.

(II): All buns are samosas.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. Only conclusion (I) follows.

 

GIVEN

 

• Statements: Some cakes are samosas; All samosas are buns.

 

SOLUTION

 

• 'Some cakes are samosas' + 'All samosas are buns' → by the standard I-A syllogism combination, Some cakes are buns is a valid conclusion → Conclusion I follows.

 

• 'All buns are samosas' would be the converse of 'All samosas are buns' — this is NOT automatically true just because all samosas are buns (some buns could be non-samosa buns) → Conclusion II does not follow.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• 'All A are B' never implies 'All B are A' — only 'Some B are A' can be concluded safely (since A itself is a subset of B, hence some of B, i.e., the A-part, are indeed A/samosas — but this only gives 'Some' about buns towards samosas, not a full statement here since it isn't asked either way).

 

NOTE

 

• 'Some X are Y' combined with 'All Y are Z' always gives 'Some X are Z' — this Some-All combination rule is one of the most frequently tested syllogism patterns.

question:
If + means -, - means x , x means ÷, ÷ means +, then what will come in place of the question mark (?) in the following equation?

19 - 16 ÷ 128 + 32 x 4 = ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. 424.

 

GIVEN

 

• Coded meanings: + means −, − means ×, × means ÷, ÷ means +. Equation: 19 − 16 ÷ 128 + 32 × 4.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Replace each symbol with its actual meaning: '−' becomes '×'; '÷' becomes '+'; '+' becomes '−'; '×' becomes '÷'.

 

• So the equation becomes: 19 × 16 + 128 − 32 ÷ 4.

 

• Apply BODMAS: 19 × 16 = 304; 32 ÷ 4 = 8.

 

• Now: 304 + 128 − 8 = 432 − 8 = 424.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Rewrite the whole equation with correct symbols first (a simple substitution table on scratch paper), then solve it as an ordinary BODMAS problem, never mixing the substitution and calculation steps together.

 

NOTE

 

• Symbol-swap questions are error-prone under time pressure — always re-verify each substituted symbol before starting the arithmetic.

question:
Based on the English alphabetical order, three of the following four letter-cluster pairs are alike in a certain way and thus form a group. Which letter-cluster pair DOES NOT belong to that group?

(Note: The odd one out is not based on the number of consonants/vowels or their position in the letter-cluster.)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. BM – FJ.

 

GIVEN

 

• Pairs: KP–ON, QL–UJ, BM–FJ, RD–VB.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Check the position-shift of each letter (A=1...Z=26) from first cluster to second cluster:

 

• KP–ON: K(11)→O(15) = +4; P(16)→N(14) = −2.

 

• QL–UJ: Q(17)→U(21) = +4; L(12)→J(10) = −2.

 

• BM–FJ: B(2)→F(6) = +4; M(13)→J(10) = −3 (breaks the pattern).

 

• RD–VB: R(18)→V(22) = +4; D(4)→B(2) = −2.

 

• Three pairs follow the consistent pattern (+4, −2); BM–FJ alone follows (+4, −3), making it the odd one out.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• For letter-cluster group questions, always convert to alphabet positions and check first-letter shift and second-letter shift separately — the group pattern usually has fixed shifts in both.

 

NOTE

 

• Even when the first-letter shift matches across all four pairs, always verify the second letter too — the odd one out can hide in either position.

question:
Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following sets.

(NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into their constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding to/subtracting from/multiplying with 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)

(2, 30, 15)

(21, 189, 9)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. (4, 40, 10).

 

GIVEN

 

• Related sets: (2, 30, 15) and (21, 189, 9).

 

SOLUTION

 

• Check the relation between the 1st and 3rd numbers, multiplied to get the 2nd: (2, 30, 15): 2 × 15 = 30 ✓ matches the middle number.

 

• (21, 189, 9): 21 × 9 = 189 ✓ matches the middle number. Pattern confirmed: 1st × 3rd = 2nd.

 

• Test each option using this rule:
